Main finding: CURA uses 20.51% less work than calibration-selected ef96 on 200 held-out queries. Post-hoc fixed ef48 matches CURA's observed 1% violation rate with 28.29% less work; ef64 also has lower observed risk and work than CURA. Exact-positive queries account for 92.59% of the original saving, while judgment-density effects remain unresolved. Available-input checks pass, but full-study validation fails because ranking-based checks and 50 scored seeds remain unavailable.
Current strongest novelty: The strongest supported contribution is a paired analysis showing that ANN-neighbor fidelity and judged-IR safety can require different budgets even when exact nDCG is positive. The full fixed frontier exposes how calibration and probe overhead affect whether that headroom yields an adaptive efficiency advantage.
Remaining blocker: Original exact top-k document IDs and HNSW document IDs for all 43 queries at all ten ef values are missing. The original subset document map, query/corpus vectors and built HNSW index needed for retrieval-only recovery are also missing; zero ranking seeds have been evaluated.
validation_explanation: Requested full-study checks fail because original rankings, same-ranking verification, FULL metric reproduction and 50 scored seeds are unavailable.
